C-SEC-EXT-GRANT-BOUND.IntentSummary: Bind each extension's incoming rights to the capability set approved at pairing time: the approved incoming capability set is captured from the registered manifest whether or not the extension is enabled and persisted beside the credential in the auth store; every incoming route — /ext/context, /ext/apply, /ext/text-insert and every /stream/* route at open and on every state change — authorizes by that stored grant instead of the live manifest; enabling an extension whose current manifest requests incoming capabilities beyond the stored grant is refused into explicit re-approval through the gallery error surface; and key replacement becomes honest — store_secret verifies the new key through the effective credential path before reporting success and a rebind additionally verifies the old key no longer validates, with keychain write failure, verification mismatch and keychain read error as distinct logged refusal states. Proven by a grant-establishing fixture, the migrated enabled_extension_passes_only_declared_capability_routes pin (mechanism moves from manifest-derived to grant-derived, meaning and statuses unchanged), grow-after-pairing and stream-without-grant refusals, the fail-closed legacy-credential pin, the honest-replace family, the gallery re-approval-surface test, and the two unchanged-meaning extensionGallery vitest suites.

Design decisions locked by this plan: (1) the approved grant persists BESIDE the secret in the auth store as a second record under the same backend family — key ext:{ext_id}:approved_grant, canonical JSON array of incoming capability names in RouteCapability::all() fixed order, memory mirror MEM_GRANTS, read precedence identical to get_secret — chosen over a registry-side grant because the registry is rebuilt by re-discovery (register overwrites state, registry.rs:89-110), so a registry-stored grant would be silently wiped or stale exactly when the manifest grows, while the auth store is the one place already keyed by extension id, already surviving restarts, and already the thing every route authenticates through; "one secret per extension id" is untouched — the grant is capability names, not a credential. (2) Grant absence (Ok(None)) and grant read failure both fail closed on every incoming route — the recorded no-migration assumption means credentials paired before this change lose incoming rights until a fresh pairing. (3) Pairing captures the grant from a new registry.peek_manifest that answers regardless of enabled state, stores the grant BEFORE the secret, and the stored set is exactly the dialog-presented incoming subset in all() order; an unregistered id stores the honest empty grant. (4) Route authorization moves wholesale to the stored grant: candidate selection keeps its current shape, the request-time manifest capability check is removed; stream enforcement lives inside authenticate_stream so validate_bearer inherits it for every state change, refusals 401 with distinct BLOCK_STREAM_GRANT_REFUSED reasons, before any session mutation or live event. (5) mt_ext_enable mints a credential with NO grant (authorizes no incoming route, spec criterion 2) and refuses enable when the current manifest requests incoming capabilities beyond the stored grant, via peek_manifest (get_manifest is enabled-only and would self-refuse); the check does its credential I/O before stream_gate per the lock-order rule that native credential I/O holds neither gate nor session lock. (6) Honest replace: store_secret verifies through get_secret (the effective credential path) and fails with memory rollback on mismatch/absence/read-error; handle_pair stores the grant first (inert until a credential exists), then the verified secret, then — rebind only — proves the prior token no longer validates; keychain write failure, verification mismatch and keychain read error are distinct logged refusal states and none reports success. Deviation note (one, deliberate): the spec enumerates an exact seven-file ObservedWriteScope; this plan appends .grace/graph/features.xml and .grace/verification/features.xml because the spec's own constraints require the GRACE surface to stay synchronized and task T-005 writes those governed files — the same extension the C-SEC-STREAM-SCOPE and C-SEC-PAIR-REBIND plans applied over their specs. Per the drafting instruction this plan carries no self-referential grace-lint MustPassCommand; the orchestrator runs current/target/final lifecycle assertions itself. Writing this draft approves neither the execution plan nor code implementation, apply/archive, commits, departure into main, manual-acceptance exceptions or release.

T-003.Title: Honest key replacement: store_secret verifies through the effective credential path and the pair verifies new-valid plus old-dead

AcceptanceCriteria.Criterion: src-tauri/src/m045_ext/auth.rs store_secret becomes verifying: it captures the previous memory value, writes the memory store and the best-effort persistent record (the BLOCK_KEYCHAIN_STORE_FAILED "(in-memory fallback active)" warning is kept verbatim for a failed keychain write), then verifies through get_secret — the effective credential path every reader uses: equal via constant_time_eq → the now-conditional BLOCK_STORE_OK and Ok(()); Ok(Some(other)) → BLOCK_STORE_VERIFY_MISMATCH and Err; Ok(None) → BLOCK_STORE_VERIFY_ABSENT and Err; Err → BLOCK_STORE_VERIFY_READ_FAILED and Err. Every failure path restores the captured previous memory value, so a refused store leaves the prior credential exactly as found; error strings carry no secret material. Callers today (handle_pair, the mt_ext_enable mint) both want this strictness; no other function in auth.rs changes behavior.

src-tauri/src/m045_ext/live_server.rs handle_pair post-approval sequence: store_grant (T-001, inert until a credential exists) → store_secret, whose Err maps to the existing 500 BLOCK_PAIR_SECRET_STORE_FAILED with the prior key intact (memory rollback plus untouched keychain) → rebind-only verification: spawn_blocking validate_token(extension_id, prior_secret) — Ok(false) proceeds, Ok(true) refuses 500 BLOCK_PAIR_OLD_KEY_STILL_VALID, Err refuses 500 BLOCK_PAIR_CREDENTIAL_VERIFY_READ_FAILED — and only then BLOCK_PAIR_OK with paired:true. First pairing requires only the new-key verification. The refused states never report success, never leave the old key displaced while claiming a working new one, and are distinct logged states: keychain write failure (BLOCK_KEYCHAIN_STORE_FAILED via store_secret), verification mismatch (BLOCK_STORE_VERIFY_MISMATCH/BLOCK_PAIR_NEW_KEY_UNVERIFIED logged at the pair when store_secret refuses a rebind), keychain read error (BLOCK_STORE_VERIFY_READ_FAILED/BLOCK_PAIR_CREDENTIAL_VERIFY_READ_FAILED). The prior-secret rebind gate, its constant-time comparison, the approval decision and both dialog descriptions are untouched; the single-record credential model makes old-key death structural once the new key verifies — the explicit old-token check is the verification the spec demands, and its refusal branch is defensive (documented in the impl notes, not forceable without mocking validate_token).

Module hygiene: dated CHANGE_SUMMARY entries in auth.rs and live_server.rs; markers paired and unique; no response body, log line or error message carries secret material or comparison lengths; no wire shape changes.
